question: I move to Saskatchewan before my spouse, who will join me later. Which facts are essential before predicting when our provincial health coverage will begin?
generated_answer:
You must be physically present in Saskatchewan. Your spouse must be physically present in Saskatchewan before being eligible for coverage under the Saskatchewan Medical Care Insurance Plan (Medavie Blue Cross administers the plan). If you have lived in Saskatchewan for at least 12 months, you are eligible for coverage on the first day of the third month following the month you arrived in the province. If you have lived in Saskatchewan for less than 12 months, you are eligible for coverage on the first day of the thirteenth month following the month you arrived in the province. III. I am moving to another country. What should I do about my health insurance? You are covered until the end of the month of departure. You may be eligible for excluded services outside Canada for up to one year. You must complete a Statement of Residence departing Canada (T1161) with the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and provide a copy to Medicare. IV. I am studying in a foreign country. How long will my health care coverage last? The Saskatchewan Medical Care Insurance Plan (Medavie Blue Cross administers the plan) will cover you for the first 12 months of your absence from Canada. To be eligible for coverage, you must be an eligible resident of Saskatchewan and in full-time attendance at an accredited educational institution outside Canada. V. I want to be covered for services provided outside Canada. What do I have to do? The Saskatchewan Medical Care Insurance Plan (Medavie Blue Cross administers the plan) will only pay benefits for necessary emergency services provided to eligible residents outside Canada. Residents are strongly encouraged to purchase supplementary health insurance to cover services which may occur while travelling outside Canada. VI. Will I be covered by the provincial health care system if I am travelling in Canada? You may be eligible for coverage under the Visiting Policy if you are temporarily in Saskatchewan and you are a visitor from another part of Canada. To be eligible for coverage under the Visiting Policy, you must meet the definition of a visitor as defined in The Saskatchewan Medical Care Insurance Act. You are not considered a visitor if you are in Saskatchewan to take up permanent residence, to attend an educational institution, to work or to conduct business. You must not be receiving or entitled to receive benefits from another province or territory. VII. Does the Saskatchewan Health Care Insurance Plan cover me outside the province but inside Canada? You may be eligible for coverage under the Visiting Policy if you are temporarily in another province/territory and you are a visitor from Saskatchewan. To be eligible for coverage under the Visiting Policy, you must meet the definition of a visitor as defined in The Saskatchewan Medical Care Insurance Act. You are not considered a visitor if you are in another province/territory to take up permanent residence, to attend an educational institution, to work or to conduct business. You must not be receiving or entitled to receive benefits from another province/territory. If you are not eligible under the Visiting Policy, you may apply for coverage as a resident under the Plan. You must meet the eligibility requirements for a resident under the Plan and elect to receive coverage under the Plan. VIII. Does the Government of Saskatchewan pay for all physician and hospital services provided outside the country? No. The Government of Saskatchewan will only pay for necessary emergency services provided outside Canada. Residents are strongly encouraged to purchase supplementary health insurance to cover services which may occur while travelling outside Canada. IX. Is there a waiting period on coverage if I am moving to Saskatchewan? If you have lived in Saskatchewan for at least 12 months, you are eligible for coverage on the first day of the third month following the month you arrived in the province. If you have lived in Saskatchewan for less than 12 months, you are eligible for coverage on the first day of the thirteenth month following the month you arrived in the province. X. What rights do I have if the Department of Health denies me coverage? You have the right to appeal the denial of coverage to a court of competent jurisdiction within the time period prescribed by the laws of that jurisdiction. If there is no time period prescribed by the laws of that jurisdiction, you have the right to appeal within six months from the date the decision was made. XI. Are there any other unique aspects to Saskatchewan's health insurance? The Saskatchewan Medical Care Insurance Plan is administered by Medavie Blue Cross Inc. on behalf of the Government of Saskatchewan. The Government of Saskatchewan establishes the benefits available under the Plan. Medavie Blue Cross Inc. is responsible for the adjudication of submitted claims, the payment of claims and the monitoring of benefit utilization. The Plan is administered under the authority of The Saskatchewan Medical Care Insurance Act and Regulations, which can be viewed at: http://www.health.gov.sk.ca/health-legislation. XII. Is there anything else I should know about my health insurance? No. XIII. Where can I get more information about health insurance in Saskatchewan? For more information on health care coverage in Saskatchewan, contact:

Medavie Blue Cross Inc. 1
